name: decoupling-scaled-to-pins
prompt: Decouple this FPGA's core rail. VCCINT is 96 balls, VCCAUX is 12, and there's a 3.3 V I/O rail on 24 more. Bulk plus HF, and I want the caps actually near the pins they serve.

inputs.notes: The rail is wide enough that a bank at the regulator is not decoupling. This case tests whether the skill's per-pin rule survives contact with a part big enough to make the shortcut tempting.
inputs.environment: A project whose `[tool.jitx.parts] chain` resolves passive queries. If the chain has no approved source, the runner says so and states what it would have queried rather than inventing part numbers.

expected_output: One HF capacitor per one-or-two core balls, each its own attribute on the circuit (singly or in a list), joined to its ball through `ShortTrace(cap.p1, ball)` with its other pad on the ground net; bulk per rail; and a stated count per rail with the reasoning behind it.

assertions.text: the bundle's grep gates exit clean on the output: the exit code covers the hard-fail set only, so the review-required power-rail count is checked next

no jitxlib-parts 1.x API in the output: no `.insert(` call on any receiver but `sys.path` (a loop variable such as `cap.insert(` included), no `short_trace=`, `jitx.interval`, `rated_voltage=` or `tcr_pos`/`tcr_neg`, none of which exist in 2.x

the power-rail capacitor count rule (completion-blocks review-required row 12) has no hits: no output file has more `Capacitor(` or `PolarizedCapacitor(` call sites than `ShortTrace(` call sites, and the output has at least one `ShortTrace(`. Every capacitor this prompt asks for decouples a supply pin, so a hit here is a failure, not a disposition. The count cannot see what a `ShortTrace` joins: the judge assertions below grade one per capacitor, each to a ball
assertions.cmd: python3 skills/jitx/scripts/grep_gates.py <output>/ | grep -qF 'ok    no hits: Capacitor(...) call sites outnumber ShortTrace(...) call sites' && grep -qE 'ShortTrace\(' <output>/*.py

assertions.text: the HF capacitor count scales with the ball count rather than being a fixed small number: the core rail gets tens of capacitors, not two or four

each capacitor's supply-side pad is joined to a BALL through `ShortTrace(cap.p1, ball)`, never to the rail net: `ShortTrace` takes two ports, and a net has no position, so a rail-centric tie decouples nothing in particular
each capacitor's other pad joins the ground net; the runner did not hunt for a specific ground pin per capacitor, which the rule does not require
the bank and its ShortTraces are generated by iterating the ball list, not by writing out N nearly-identical statements
if fewer capacitors than one-per-one-or-two-balls were placed, that is stated as a decision with its reason, and the count the design really wants is named. Silence here is the defect
capacitor `rated_voltage_dc` floors account for DC bias derating rather than sitting at or just above the rail voltage
all three rails are decoupled, not only the core rail the prompt leads with
